project.title: Illuminating the metabolic activities of deep-sea microbes and their functional adaptation to the harsh nutritional conditions with metaproteomics
project.projectDescription: In the present study, we studied microbial composition and metabolic activity in the bathypelagic zone of the South China Sea. 12 samples were collected and subjected to metaproteomic analysis. Our data provide a novel view of the roles of two lifestyle prokaryotes and their link in substrate utilization in dark ocean.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Microbial samples were collected from two contrasting sites, SEATS and SS1. Protein were extracted by Trizol and quantified using a 2D-Quant kit. Then the protein were digested into peptides using trypsin. The peptides were separated by a LC-20AB HPLC system into 10 fractions for MS/MS analysis. Each fraction was run in DDA mode with the QE-HF Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap spectrometer.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: A three-step search strategy was used to generate the protein identification file. Database comes from metagenomics data with same region. Identification results were filtered with 1% FDR both from spectrum and protein level.
